# RIGOR — the four styles, measured

**Generated by `tests/rigor_styles.js` on 2026-08-15 at 48000 Hz.**

That sentence was false from round 7 until round 8: the file it names did not
exist, and these numbers were produced once by hand and then edited by
successive rounds until the prose disagreed with the code. The generator now
exists. Run it and paste, or diff it against this file.

```bash
node tests/rigor_styles.js
```

All four driven identically: threshold −30, 4:1, hard knee, 20 ms attack,
400 ms release, auto-release off, on a −10 dBFS step. The only difference is
the topology.

| Style | Topology | Detector | Envelope on | Peak decay | Level-dep. attack | Settled GR | Time to 63.2% |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **fresh** | feedforward | peak | gain | 15 ms | — | −15.00 dB | 20.0 ms |
| **settling** | **feedback** | RMS 10 ms | **level** | 15 ms | **yes** | −8.86 dB | 15.7 ms |
| **spasm** | feedforward | peak | gain | **2 ms** | — | −15.00 dB | 20.0 ms |
| **repose** | feedforward | RMS 50 ms | gain | 15 ms | — | −15.00 dB | 36.6 ms |

## Four paths, at last

**Four topologies across four styles**, as of round 8.

| Path | Styles |
|---|---|
| feedforward · peak · gain-smoothed · peak decay 15 ms | **Fresh** |
| feedback · RMS 10 ms · level-smoothed · level-dependent attack | **Settling** |
| feedforward · peak · gain-smoothed · **peak decay 2 ms** | **Spasm** |
| feedforward · RMS 50 ms · gain-smoothed | **Repose** |

| Pair | Same path? | Renders identically? |
|---|---|---|
| fresh / settling | no | no |
| fresh / spasm | no | no |
| fresh / repose | no | no |
| settling / spasm | no | no |
| settling / repose | no | no |
| spasm / repose | no | no |

## What round 8 changed, and the trap in this table

For five rounds this document said Fresh and Spasm were **the same signal
path** — feedforward, peak-detecting, gain-smoothed — differing only in the
defaults written into a case file. That was true, and it was measured, and it
was the right call to record it rather than gloss it.

Round 8 gave Spasm the differentiator this document proposed: **its own
peak-follower decay, 2 ms against the house 15 ms.** A short decay lets the
follower fall away between transients, so each new hit is seen at close to
its full height instead of riding a partly-charged follower. That is the
punch character, and it is now a path property rather than a preset.

**But look at the step-response columns above.** Fresh and Spasm still read
identically: −15.00 dB settled, 20.0 ms to 63.2%. A DC step never lets the
follower decay, because the level never drops — so the one measurement this
document was built on is blind to the one difference that was just added.

That is why the render column exists. Driven with **noise**, Fresh and Spasm
now differ sample-for-sample, and the generator checks every pair both ways
and flags any disagreement between "same path" and "renders identically".
The lesson is worth more than the feature: **a step response is not a
sufficient probe of a compressor's identity**, and a document that measures
one thing while claiming something broader is how this file came to assert
the opposite of the code for five rounds.

On a 200 Hz tone the two now settle to measurably different reduction —
Fresh −17.899 dB against Spasm −17.712 dB — because the 2 ms follower falls
further between cycles, reads a lower average level, and so compresses less
on sustain. Transient-forward, exactly as wanted.

## What the numbers say

Repose is slower to 63.2% (36.6 ms against a requested 20) because its 50 ms
RMS detector has to fill before the gain computer sees the level at all — the
detector's own time constant adds to the envelope's.

**Settling** is the outlier and should be. It smooths the level rather than
the gain, and its attack coefficient is recomputed from the current
overshoot, so a harder hit grabs faster. That is what an optical cell does
and it is why the figure moves. Its settled reduction is smaller because a
feedback detector reads the already-compressed output.

## Per-style defaults

Written into a case file when you pick the style, and freely overridable
afterwards. These are **defaults**, not path properties — changing one does
not make a style a different compressor.

| Style | Ratio | Knee | Attack | Release | Auto-release |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fresh | 4:1 | 6 dB | 10 ms | 200 ms | off |
| settling | 3:1 | 9 dB | 25 ms | 300 ms | on |
| spasm | 6:1 | 0 dB | 0.5 ms | 80 ms | on |
| repose | 2:1 | 18 dB | 30 ms | 400 ms | on |
